Retrieval note: Fetched via Exa 2026-07-20. Published 2026-07-17. APPROVED SOURCE (independent.co.uk).

Headline: "Farage demands immediate election saying Burnham has no mandate for power".

Nigel Farage (Reform UK leader) has demanded an immediate general election as he claimed Andy Burnham had no mandate to run the country. Speaking at the CPAC UK conference in London.
Quotes (Farage):
- "He comes in with absolutely no mandate of any kind at all, none."
- "There must be an immediate general election so the country can decide the future."
- "Nothing will get better under Andy Burnham."
- "He says he wants to have the biggest change of direction in politics in 40 years, outside of 25,000 voters in Makerfield he has literally no mandate for this at all."
- Branded Burnham "the great chameleon of British politics", "capable of being all things to all people".
- Claimed if Reform fails to win the next election Britain risks "turning into a third world country" within 10 years; predicted a "historic upset".
Farage is himself fighting a by-election in Clacton after resigning as an MP.

Cross-ref (Independent, 2026-07-17, b3017213): "Farage says 'nothing will get better under Burnham' as he calls for general election" — same quotes.
Context (BBC / earlier, gbnews 2026-06-22): Both Farage and Badenoch called for a snap election when Starmer resigned. Badenoch's line then: a general election needed if Burnham cannot fund the Defence Investment Plan.
